documentationDialog.gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
documentationDialog.gettingStarted.welco: Welcome to {productName}, a Bible study application.
documentationDialog.gettingStarted.layou: The application is divided into two main areas:
Bible Pane (left) -- The primary reading area. This displays Bible text with verse numbers, navigation controls, and a translation selector.

Study & Notes Pane (right) -- A tabbed panel that holds commentaries, dictionaries, books, notes, documents, journal entries, prayer lists, and search results. You can collapse this pane to give the Bible text full width.
documentationDialog.gettingStarted.first: Use the book/chapter selector in the Bible pane header to navigate to any passage.
Select a Bible translation from the dropdown at the top-left of the Bible pane.
Explore the tabs on the right pane to view commentaries, notes, dictionaries, and more.
Try searching by clicking the search bar at the top of the window or pressing Ctrl+L.
Right-click any verse to access the context menu with options for copying, highlighting, and note-taking.
documentationDialog.gettingStarted.sessi: Your work is automatically saved as a session. Sessions remember your open passages, commentary tabs, notes, and panel positions. The application will restore your previous session when you next launch it.
documentationDialog.biblePane.title: Bible Pane
documentationDialog.biblePane.intro: The Bible pane displays Bible text, and includes tools for navigation, display customization, and highlighting and underlining.
documentationDialog.biblePane.navItem1: Use the Book selector dropdown to choose a Bible book, then select a chapter number.
documentationDialog.biblePane.navItem2: Click the left/right arrows in the header to move to the previous or next chapter.
documentationDialog.biblePane.navItem3: Use <kbd>Alt+Left</kbd> and <kbd>Alt+Right</kbd> to navigate chapters with the keyboard.
documentationDialog.biblePane.navItem4: Click a verse number to select it. The selected verse is highlighted and linked to commentary and notes.
documentationDialog.biblePane.translatio: The dropdown at the top-left of the Bible pane lets you switch between installed Bible translations. Modules with a language prefix (e.g., [ESP]) are in a different language from your primary UI language.
documentationDialog.biblePane.displayMod: The Bible pane supports three display modes, selectable from the pane header:
Simple -- Clean reading view with only the text. Best for focused reading.
Standard -- A more traditional display with verse numbers on the left and each verse with its own line. Good for general study.
Study -- Study mode with options for interlinear Greek/Hebrew text (if the translation has that info) and cross-references and commentary links displayed alongside each verse.
documentationDialog.biblePane.parallelBo: Click the Parallel View button in the Bible pane header to display multiple translations side by side for the same passage.
documentationDialog.biblePane.textSettin: Right-click the Bible pane header or use the text settings icon to adjust:
Font family (serif options optimized for Bible reading)
Red-letter text for words of Christ (on/off)
documentationDialog.search.title: Search
documentationDialog.search.intro: You can search across all installed modules.
documentationDialog.search.quickBody: The search bar at the top of the window (<kbd>Ctrl+L</kbd>) displays suggestions and results live, as you type, for keyword searches. By default, it searches the currently active Bible translation.
documentationDialog.search.quickItem1: Type a word or phrase to search for matching verses.
documentationDialog.search.quickItem2: As you type, live suggestions appear showing matching verses.
documentationDialog.search.quickItem3: Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to execute the full search and open the Search Results tab.
documentationDialog.search.quickItem4: Type a Bible reference (e.g., "John 3:16") to navigate directly to that passage.
documentationDialog.search.advancedBody: Open the Advanced Search dialog from the search bar or Search Results tab for more options:
documentationDialog.search.advancedScope: Scope -- Search the current module, all Bibles, all modules, or a specific range of books.
documentationDialog.search.advancedWhole: Whole Word -- Only match complete words, not partial matches.
documentationDialog.search.advancedFuzzy: Fuzzy Search -- Find words with similar spelling (configurable distance). Useful when you are not sure of exact wording.
documentationDialog.search.advancedProxi: Proximity Search -- Find two or more words that appear near each other within a specified number of words.
documentationDialog.search.advancedAutoF: Auto-Fuzzy -- Automatically enables fuzzy matching when fewer than 3 results are found.
documentationDialog.search.resultsBody: Results are displayed in the Search Results tab on the right pane. Features include:
documentationDialog.search.resultsItem1: A distribution graph showing which Bible books contain the most matches.
documentationDialog.search.resultsItem2: Click any result to navigate the Bible pane to that verse.
documentationDialog.search.resultsItem3: Results show the matching text with the search term highlighted in context.
documentationDialog.search.resultsItem4: The result count and search time are displayed at the top.
documentationDialog.search.savedBody: You can save frequently used searches for quick access. Saved searches remember the query, search type, scope, and options.
documentationDialog.commentaries.title: Commentaries
documentationDialog.commentaries.intro: The Commentary tab in the right pane displays commentary entries that correspond to the currently selected verse in the Bible pane.
documentationDialog.commentaries.viewing: Select a verse in the Bible pane -- the Commentary tab automatically updates to show relevant entries.
Use the commentary tabs to switch between different installed commentaries.
Each commentary entry includes the referenced verse range and the commentary text.
documentationDialog.commentaries.navItem: The commentary pane shows previous/next arrows to move to the nearest verse that has commentary content.
Use the tree view to browse the full table of contents of a commentary.
Scripture references within commentary text are clickable and will navigate the Bible pane to that passage.
documentationDialog.commentaries.managin: Install or remove commentaries through the Module Manager (File > Module Manager). You can open multiple commentary tabs simultaneously for comparison.
documentationDialog.highlights.title: Highlights & Annotations
documentationDialog.highlights.intro: Highlights let you color-code verses for quick visual identification. Annotations let you attach notes directly to specific verses.
documentationDialog.highlights.highlight: Select one or more verses by clicking on them in the Bible pane.
Right-click to open the context menu and choose Highlight.
Choose a highlight color from the palette (yellow, green, blue, pink, orange, and more).
The verse text will be displayed with the selected background color.
documentationDialog.highlights.tip: You can also use the floating annotation toolbar that appears when you select text within a verse.
documentationDialog.highlights.removingB: To remove a highlight, right-click the highlighted verse and choose Remove Highlight/Underline from the context menu, or select a different color to change it.
documentationDialog.highlights.colorsBod: Each color can represent a different category or theme in your study. For example, you might use yellow for promises, green for commands, and blue for prophecy. The system you use is up to you.
documentationDialog.notes.title: Notes
documentationDialog.notes.intro: The application provides several types of note-taking, all accessible from tabs in the right pane.
documentationDialog.notes.verseNotesBody: Verse notes are attached to a specific Bible verse. They appear in the "Verse Notes" tab and automatically sync to the selected verse.
documentationDialog.notes.verseNotesItem: Select a verse in the Bible pane, then switch to the Verse Notes tab.
Click New Note or right-click a verse and choose Add Note.
Type your note in the rich text editor. Your note is saved automatically.
Verses with notes are indicated by a small note icon in the Bible pane.
documentationDialog.notes.documentsBody: Documents are longer-form notes not tied to a specific verse. Use them for sermon outlines, research papers, topical studies, or extended writing.
documentationDialog.notes.documentsItem1: Switch to the Documents tab in the right pane.
documentationDialog.notes.documentsItem2: Click New Document to create a new document with a title.
documentationDialog.notes.documentsItem3: The rich text editor supports formatting: bold, italic, headings, lists, and more.
documentationDialog.notes.documentsItem4: Documents are saved automatically and can be organized with tags.
documentationDialog.notes.journalBody: The Journal tab provides a date-organized space for daily devotional notes and reflections. Each journal entry is automatically stamped with the current date.
documentationDialog.notes.editorIntro: All note types use a rich text editor with the following formatting options:
documentationDialog.prayer.title: Prayer Lists
documentationDialog.prayer.intro: Prayer lists help you organize prayer requests. Access them from the Prayer tab in the right pane.
documentationDialog.prayer.managingItem1: Create multiple prayer lists to organize requests by category.
documentationDialog.prayer.managingItem2: Each list has a name and optional color for visual identification.
documentationDialog.prayer.managingItem3: Switch between lists using the list selector dropdown at the top of the Prayer tab.
documentationDialog.prayer.itemsItem1: Click New Prayer to add a prayer request to the current list.
documentationDialog.prayer.itemsItem2: Each prayer has a title and content field for details.
documentationDialog.prayer.itemsItem3: If a prayer is marked as Answered, it moves to a separate Answered section.
documentationDialog.prayer.itemsItem4: Reorder prayers by dragging them within the list.
documentationDialog.prayer.itemsItem5: You may delete prayers that you do not need.
documentationDialog.prayer.tip: Link Bible verses to your prayers for quick reference to Scripture that relates to your prayer requests.
documentationDialog.dictionaries.title: Dictionaries & Lexicons
documentationDialog.dictionaries.intro: Dictionaries and lexicons provide word definitions, Strong's concordance entries, and linguistic data for deeper study.
documentationDialog.dictionaries.usingIt: Switch to the Dictionary tab in the right pane.
Select a dictionary from the dropdown (e.g., Strong's Greek, Strong's Hebrew, or a Bible dictionary).
Browse entries alphabetically or search for a specific term.
Click any entry to see its full definition.
documentationDialog.dictionaries.strongs: When in Study display mode, Strong's numbers appear beneath the Greek or Hebrew words in the interlinear display. Click a Strong's number to look up its entry in the dictionary.
Greek numbers are prefixed with G (e.g., G26 = agape, love).
Hebrew numbers are prefixed with H (e.g., H430 = Elohim, God).
The dictionary entry shows the word, transliteration, pronunciation, definition, and usage examples.
documentationDialog.dictionaries.occurre: When viewing a dictionary entry, you can see all Bible verses where that word appears. This is especially useful for word studies to understand how a particular Greek or Hebrew word is used throughout Scripture.
documentationDialog.studyMode.title: Study Mode & Interlinear
documentationDialog.studyMode.intro: Study Mode provides the deepest level of analysis for Bible text, including interlinear displays, morphology, and Strong's concordance integration.
documentationDialog.studyMode.enablingBo: Select Study from the display mode selector in the Bible pane header. This mode requires a Bible translation that includes interlinear data (such as a Greek or Hebrew interlinear module).
documentationDialog.studyMode.interlinea: In Study Mode, each word is displayed in a stacked layout showing:
Original language word -- The Greek or Hebrew text.
Strong's number -- Click to look up in the dictionary.
Morphology code -- Part of speech, tense, mood, case, etc.
documentationDialog.studyMode.morphology: Parts of speech are color-coded for quick identification:
documentationDialog.studyMode.xrefBody: Study Mode shows cross-reference markers next to verses. Click these to see related passages. You can also create your own cross-references.
documentationDialog.copyExport.title: Copy & Export
documentationDialog.copyExport.intro: You can copy and export Bible text flexibly, in several different formats.
documentationDialog.copyExport.copyingIt: Right-click a verse and choose Copy to copy it with the default format.
Choose Copy with Options for the full copy dialog where you can customize the format.
Select multiple verses by clicking a range, then copy them all at once.
documentationDialog.copyExport.formatInt: The Copy Options dialog lets you customize how copied text is formatted:
documentationDialog.copyExport.formatIte: Format templates -- Choose from preset formats or create your own.
Verse range -- Adjust the range of verses to copy directly in the dialog.
A live preview shows exactly what will be placed on the clipboard.
documentationDialog.copyExport.exporting: Go to File > Export My Notes to export your notes, highlights, and other user data. This creates a backup file that can be restored later.
documentationDialog.copyExport.backupBod: The Backup & Restore feature (File > Export My Notes) creates an encrypted, password-protected backup of all your user data including notes, highlights, and sessions. You can restore from a backup using Merge mode (keeps existing data) or Replace mode (replaces all data).
documentationDialog.moduleManager.title: Module Manager
documentationDialog.moduleManager.intro: The Module Manager lets you install, update, and remove Bible translations, commentaries, dictionaries, and other study resources.
documentationDialog.moduleManager.openin: Go to File > Module Manager to open it. The dialog shows available and installed modules.
documentationDialog.moduleManager.instal: Switch to the Available tab to browse modules from configured repositories.
Use the filter buttons to narrow by type (Bibles, Commentaries, Dictionaries, Books).
Use the search box to find specific modules by name.
Click Install on any module to download and install it.
A progress indicator shows download status for active installations.
documentationDialog.moduleManager.managi: Switch to the Installed tab to see all currently installed modules.
Click Uninstall to remove a module you no longer need.
Check for updates to keep your modules current.
Rebuild the search index for a module if search results seem incomplete.
documentationDialog.moduleManager.fromFi: You can also install modules from local files. Click the Install from File button and select a module database file (.db) from your computer.
documentationDialog.shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
documentationDialog.shortcuts.intro: Keyboard shortcuts can help speed up your use of the app.  Below is the complete reference.
documentationDialog.shortcuts.macTip: On macOS, replace Ctrl with Cmd for all shortcuts listed above.
documentationDialog.tips.title: Tips & Tricks
documentationDialog.tips.navItem1: Type a verse reference directly into the search bar to jump straight to it (e.g., "Romans 8:28").
documentationDialog.tips.navItem2: The Bible pane remembers your navigation history within a session. Or use chapter arrows to move back and forth within a book.
documentationDialog.tips.navItem3: Collapse the right pane for a more focused reading layout, then expand it when you would like to see the study tools again.
documentationDialog.tips.workflowItem1: Start with a passage in Simple mode for reading, then switch to Study mode when you want more study details.
documentationDialog.tips.workflowItem2: Click on Strong's numbers in Study mode to see original Greek and Hebrew words.
documentationDialog.tips.workflowItem3: Use cross-references to follow theme "threads" across the whole Bible.
documentationDialog.tips.workflowItem4: Create personal cross-references if you would like.
documentationDialog.tips.organizationIte: Create your own verse highlighting color system.
Organize notes with tags so you can find related notes across different passages.
Create collections for topical studies, sermon series, or reading plans.
Use the Journal tab for daily reflections -- entries are automatically date-stamped.
documentationDialog.tips.safetyItem1: Create regular backups of your data through File > Export My Notes.
documentationDialog.tips.safetyItem2: Backups are encrypted with your password -- keep the password safe.
documentationDialog.tips.safetyItem3: Sessions auto-save your UI state, so you will not lose your place if the app closes unexpectedly.
backupRestoreDialog.restoreYourDataFromA: Restore your data from a previously created backup file.
backupRestoreDialog.keepsExistingDataOve: Keeps existing data, overwrites duplicates from backup

backupRestoreDialog.replaceWarning: Warning: Replace mode will delete all existing user data before importing. This cannot be undone.

moduleDisclaimer.digest.caution: Computers sometimes make mistakes in summarizing, and commentaries sometimes have false doctrines.

moduleDisclaimer.generated.caution: Automatically generated text can contain mistakes.  Always use the Bible itself as your final authority.
onboarding.tour.bible.title: The Bible pane
onboarding.tour.bible.body: This is where you can read the Bible itself. Use the book and chapter controls at the top to move around, or click any verse so that the study tools synchornize to that verse.
onboarding.tour.study.title: Study tools follow along
onboarding.tour.study.body: Commentaries, cross-references, dictionaries and topics all track the verse you have selected.
onboarding.tour.search.title: General search box
onboarding.tour.search.body: Type a reference such as John 3:16 to jump straight to it, or type words and phrases to search the text of every module you have open.
onboarding.tour.addPane.title: Build your own workspace
onboarding.tour.addPane.body: The plus button adds a pane to any group. Drag a pane by its tab to move or split it, and close anything you are not using — the arrangement is remembered for next time.
onboarding.tour.finish.title: That is the end of the tour!
onboarding.tour.finish.body: You can learn as you go.  Empty panes should contain explanation text of what to do, and you can reopen this tour any time from the Help menu!
onboarding.welcome.message: By default, the Bible is on one side, and your study tools are on the other.  Pick a verse and everything else follows along.
onboarding.language.title: Choose your language
onboarding.language.intro: This sets the language of the app itself. You can change it later in Preferences.
onboarding.language.packsEmpty: No study content is available for this language yet.
onboarding.language.packsEmptyHint: You can browse and install modules any time from Tools → Module Manager.
onboarding.language.packsIntro: These collections are recommended for your language. Install them from Tools → Module Manager, where you can review each item’s licence first.
onboarding.empty.workspace.description: Every part of this app lives in a pane you can move, split or close. You can start with a Bible pane and then add tools as you need them.
onboarding.empty.book.title: Read a book about the Bible
onboarding.empty.book.description: Book modules are complete works, such as church history, theology, or classic devotional writing, with their own table of contents.
onboarding.empty.bookShelf.title: Your bookshelf
onboarding.empty.bookShelf.description: This pane holds whole books you read straight through. Open one and it becomes a tab here.
onboarding.empty.dictionaryShelf.title: Your dictionaries
onboarding.empty.dictionaryShelf.descrip: Open a dictionary and it becomes a tab here, ready for a word, a name, or a Strong’s number.
onboarding.empty.dictionary.title: Look up a word in its original language
onboarding.empty.dictionary.description: A dictionary module explains the Hebrew and Greek behind the English, with definitions, pronunciation and the other places each word appears.
onboarding.empty.dictionary.hint: Once one is open you can search by English word or by Strong’s number, such as G25.
onboarding.empty.dictionaryEntry.title: Look up a word in {dictionary}
onboarding.empty.dictionaryEntry.descrip: Type into the box above and matching entries appear as you type, so a half-remembered spelling is enough. Strong’s numbers work too — try G25 or H430.
onboarding.empty.notes.title: Somewhere to write
onboarding.empty.notes.description: Notes are ordinary files in a folder you chose, so sermon outlines, lesson prep and journal entries stay yours — readable and backed up outside this app.
onboarding.empty.verseNotes.title: Notes on individual verses land here
onboarding.empty.verseNotes.description: Right-click any verse in the Bible pane and add a note; it is filed here automatically, under the reference it belongs to.
onboarding.empty.topics.title: Nothing to show for these sources
onboarding.empty.topics.description: No topics came back from the sources currently selected. Turn another source back on above, or search for a subject by name.
onboarding.empty.topicsNoModules.title: Find every passage on a subject
onboarding.empty.topicsNoModules.descrip: A topical index is a subject catalogue of the Bible: pick something like forgiveness or covenant and it lists the passages that speak to it. Install one to use this pane.
onboarding.empty.commentary.title: Read what others have written on this passage
onboarding.empty.commentary.description: A commentary walks verse by verse through the text — explaining context, language and meaning. Opened here, it follows the passage you are reading.

diagnostics.privacyBlurb:
What we send:
  - App version, operating system, and processor architecture
  - The error itself (message and source-mapped stack trace)
  - Names of recent app operations (method names only, no arguments)
  - A memory usage reading

What we never send:
  - Your notes, highlights, or any content you've written
  - Your search queries or reading history
  - Which Bible translations or modules you have installed
  - File paths, your username, or anything that identifies you
  - Your IP address, timezone, or locale

documentationDialog.bookmarks.intro: Bookmarks let you save passages to come back to.  You may name them, move their locations, and rearrange how they are displayed in the Bookmarks section.
documentationDialog.bookmarks.savingItem: Click a verse, then open the ribbon in the Bible pane toolbar and choose Add Current Verse — or just press Ctrl+D.
Shift-click to select a passage first, and the whole passage is saved.
Or right-click a verse and choose Add to Bookmarks.
